summary: Matt Welsh presents AI.JSX, an open-source TypeScript framework for building reactive AI applications, announced at the AI Engineer Summit 2023. The core problem is that building and deploying high-quality LLM apps remains hard, involving vector databases, context window limits, RAG stacks, and tool integration. Welsh argues JavaScript developers—the largest developer community—have been underserved by existing Python-centric AI tooling. AI.JSX is positioned as 'React for LLMs,' where components render to the LLM instead of the DOM. Unlike React rendering to a browser DOM, AI.JSX renders a tree of JSX nodes asynchronously and in parallel as streams to LLMs, enabling powerful composition patterns. A hello world example shows a ChatCompletion component receiving a user message prompt. A make-story component with three child components runs concurrent LLM calls streaming tokens in parallel. Wrapper components like KidSafe demonstrate constraining output by wrapping any child component with a system message. Tool calling uses a UseTools component providing LLMs access to external APIs like GitHub's GraphQL endpoint. RAG is implemented in approximately 10 lines using a DocsQA component. AI.JSX supports any model provider, multiple vector databases, custom tools, and AI-generated UI components. The Fixie cloud platform provides managed RAG pipelines, conversational state management, and optimized LLM interfaces. Welsh previews real-time bidirectional voice interaction built with AI.JSX, contrasting it with ChatGPT's four-to-five-second voice latency. A pre-recorded demo features a fictional 'Dr. Donut' drive-through where the AI takes a customer's order in real time, handles off-topic questions gracefully, and computes a total. Welsh emphasizes the demo is unstaged, untrimmed, and unspeeded-up, available to try at voice.fixie.ai. The demo runs on the full Fixie platform backend, and Welsh invites developers to build similar experiences, noting Fixie is hiring.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Welsh introduces the problem: building and deploying high-quality LLM apps is hard, involving vector databases, context limits, RAG stacks, and tool sets. Fixie aims to solve this for developers who would rather not solve these problems themselves.

sections.title: AI.JSX Announcement and TypeScript Rationale
sections.summary: Welsh announces AI.JSX with a dramatic reveal, describing it as 'React for LLMs' in TypeScript. He argues JavaScript developers are underserved by Python-centric AI tooling and that the larger JS community should have access to AI development tools.

sections.title: Hello World and Component Basics
sections.summary: A hello world example shows a ChatCompletion component with a user message prompt. AI.JSX features include any model/provider support, full React integration, built-in RAG, custom tools, and AI-generated UI components. Components take children as parameters, similar to React.

sections.title: Parallel Streaming and Composition
sections.summary: AI.JSX renders a tree of nodes asynchronously and in parallel to the LLM rather than the DOM. A MakeStory component with three child components runs concurrent LLM calls streaming tokens in parallel. The KidSafe wrapper component demonstrates constraining output by wrapping any child component with a system message.

sections.title: Tool Calling and RAG Implementation
sections.summary: Tool calling uses a UseTools component with a record of tools, demonstrated with the GitHub GraphQL API. RAG is implemented in approximately 10 lines using a DocsQA component that retrieves relevant chunks from a vector database corpus and injects them into the system message alongside the user query.

sections.title: Fixie Platform and Voice Interaction Preview
sections.summary: The Fixie cloud platform offers managed RAG pipelines, conversational state management, optimized LLM interfaces, no-code and code-based development, and easy web embedding. Welsh previews real-time bidirectional voice interaction built with AI.JSX, contrasting its performance with ChatGPT voice demos that have a four-to-five-second latency gap.

sections.title: Voice Demo and Conclusion
sections.summary: Welsh shows a pre-recorded real-time voice demo of a fictional 'Dr. Donut' drive-through where the AI takes a customer's order, recommends items, handles an off-topic question about LLMs gracefully, and computes a total. He emphasizes the demo is unstaged, untrimmed, and unspeeded-up, available at voice.fixie.ai, and runs on the full Fixie platform backend. Welsh concludes by encouraging attendees to try it, noting Fixie is hiring.
